title: Student Activities Room Rules (SAMPLE)
author: Exec board
text: SAMPLE: replace with the official Texas A&M Student Activities text at handoff. Room and facility reservations go through the Student Activities portal. Requests must be filed at least 14 days before the event. Late requests can be denied; an adviser contact in Student Activities can sometimes push a late request through. Events with food need the food-service approval box checked on the request. Keep the confirmation email; security will ask for it on the day.

title: Funds and Signature Rules (SAMPLE)
author: Exec board
text: SAMPLE: replace with the official Texas A&M student-organization finance policy at handoff. Any single expense over $500 needs the faculty advisor's signature, and the advisor needs about five working days to sign. Sponsorship money is deposited to the club account, never to a personal account. Keep every receipt; reimbursements without a receipt are refused. Dues are $120 per member per year.

title: Constitution
author: Exec board
text: Officer eligibility: a member can run for office if dues are paid for the current year and general-meeting attendance is at least 70%. Eligibility is checked at the eligibility review held before elections (this year: Nov 20, online). Officers serve one academic year. Exit interviews with the incoming officer are required before an officer's term ends. The president calls general meetings; the secretary keeps minutes and files them in Docs.

title: Spring Gala Recap
author: Priya Nair
text: Spring Gala 2025, Hilton ballroom, 92 attendees. Budget $4,800, actual $4,520. Funding: $3,000 from Lone Star Machining (main sponsor), $1,100 in tickets, $700 from dues reserves. WORKED: sponsor landed, strong turnout, food on time, the photo wall. DID NOT WORK: decor ran about $300 over budget; sponsor outreach started 10 weeks out, which was just barely enough. NEXT TIME: start sponsor outreach 14 weeks out, set a hard decor cap before ordering, and send the sponsor thank-you letter within a week.

title: Robo-Rumble Recap
author: Priya Nair
text: Robo-Rumble 2025, Rec Center, February 2025. About 60 attendees. Budget $2,500, actual $2,310. WORKED: brackets ran smoothly on Challonge; alumni judges were the highlight and drew the biggest crowd on the final match. DID NOT WORK: the room request was filed only 9 days out and was denied once before Ms. Reyes in Student Activities pushed it through. NEXT TIME: file the room request 14+ days out (target 3 weeks), invite alumni judges early, order trophies and medals before the last two weeks, and plan pizza as a food fallback if the caterer cannot deliver in time.

title: Fall Kickoff Minutes
author: Luis Ortega
text: Fall Kickoff, September 2025, ZACH atrium. 74 attendees, budget $1,000, actual $980. Tacos from Brazos Smokehouse were a hit and the sign-up rate was the best in years. DID NOT WORK: ran out of name tags and drinks. NEXT TIME: bring 100 name tags and double the drinks. Have a QR code sign-up sheet at the door; the paper sheet had a line.

title: Workshop Series Notes
author: Priya Nair
text: Workshop series, October 2025, ZACH 244. Four sessions, 38 total turnout, budget $1,000, actual $950. WORKED: Soldering 101 filled in two days; every part provided, no experience needed. DID NOT WORK: parts for week 3 arrived late and the kits were short. NEXT TIME: order parts 3 weeks ahead, order 10% extra, and keep the soldering sessions to 20 people.

title: Vendor Contacts
author: Maya Chen
text: Brazos Smokehouse (food): ask for Dana Ortiz, 979-555-0142. Order at least 3 weeks ahead and ask for the student-org rate; it saved about 12% last year. Lone Star Machining: main sponsor, contributed $3,000 to the Gala and $3,750 this fall; send a thank-you letter after every event. Ms. Reyes, Student Activities: room approvals, can sometimes push a late request. Challonge: free bracket tool used for Robo-Rumble.

title: Budget FY25
author: Maya Chen
text: FY25 spend by event: Spring Gala $4,520, Robo-Rumble 2025 $2,310, Fall Kickoff $980, Workshops $950. Total $8,760. Food is the largest category at roughly 48% of spend. Income: sponsorships $7,500, dues $5,160 (43 members x $120), fundraisers $2,100, total $14,760. Rule of thumb that held up: budget each event at about 5% over last year's actual and keep a reserve of at least $2,000.

title: Treasurer Reflection
author: Ravi Shah
text: Written by the outgoing treasurer. Loose ends left: thank-you letters to Lone Star Machining and closing the old Venmo account. Unwritten rules: the advisor signs anything over $500 and that takes about five days. Dues reminders work best as a text the Monday after a general meeting. Reconcile dues against the membership sheet before the first meeting of the semester. Sponsor outreach should start at 14 weeks, not 10.

title: Officer Playbook
author: Jordan Ellis
text: How the club runs. Book rooms through Student Activities 14+ days ahead. Every event gets: a budget approved by the exec board, a run-of-show checklist, a promo post approved the week before, and a recap doc filed within a week. Alumni judges and speakers drew the best turnout. Rule: if a plan has no recap from a past year, ask the officer who ran the closest event before spending money.

title: Secretary Handoff
author: Luis Ortega
text: Secretary handoff filed Oct 28. Minutes live in the shared Drive under Minutes/<year>. Attendance is tracked on the Membership Sheet after each general meeting. The eligibility review needs attendance totals two days before it happens. Send the agenda 24 hours before every meeting.

title: Membership Sheet
author: Luis Ortega
text: 45 active members this fall; 43 have paid dues, 2 owe (Sam Whitaker, Eli Park). Average attendance over the last 6 meetings is 76%. Eligible to run for office: dues paid and 70% attendance. Tracked members are listed in People.

title: Marketing Notes
author: Tara Brooks
text: What worked on social: event-day posts with a photo of a bot beat text graphics about 3 to 1. Short captions that name the room and the free food drive the most sign-ups. Thursday 10am is the strongest posting slot. WHAT DID NOT WORK: long captions and posts without a date. Post the promo one week out and again two days out.
